visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1’s binary-search trace and complexity visuals are largely positionally and mathematically correct, while Lesson 2’s trace diagram misplaces/combines the mid, low, and high markers around the 56/38/45 step, creating an inconsistent representation of the algorithm state.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons have absent gate specs and absent plan JSON, so neither provides any functioning checkpoints or interactive questions.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has severe garbled and unnatural phrasing throughout, but Lesson 2 has no available narration transcript at all, so Lesson 1 is marginally better because it at least contains some intelligible narration while Lesson 2 is absent.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 at least provides a narration sequence that could potentially be aligned, while Lesson 2 has no transcript or timing data at all, though Lesson 1 also lacks the beat/cue timing needed to verify sync reliably.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 is garbled and incomplete in places but still conveys the core binary-search idea, example trace, halving intuition, and O(log n) comparison, whereas Lesson 2 has no transcript or teaching content to evaluate and therefore provides no conceptual explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is much more legible, consistently styled, and slide-composed despite the distracting cursor/subtitle/player overlays, whereas Lesson 2 has tiny low-contrast text, dim/unclear diagrams, awkward off-center sparse layouts, and a visible text glitch around the binary-search label.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: five of the six dimension agents favored it, including high-confidence wins in visual accuracy (0.86), concept accuracy (0.95), and polish (0.78). The only non-win was interactivity, where both lessons tied because neither included functioning checkpoints or plan/gate specs. Lesson 1 has notable issues—garbled narration, incomplete sync evidence, and some distracting overlays—but it still provides usable binary-search visuals, some intelligible narration, and a core conceptual explanation. Lesson 2 is substantially weaker due to an incorrect/inconsistent trace diagram, absent narration/transcript, no teaching content to evaluate, and poor visual polish.
